subject: Framework for Aboriginal Languages and Torres Strait Islander Languages (First-Language Learner Pathway F-10)

outcomes.text: with support, recognise and communicate meaning in [Language]
explore, with support, language features of [Language], making connections between [Language] and English
identify connections between language and culture
exchange greetings and personal introductions, and respond to instructions and routines
participate in a range of guided, play-based language activities, using modelled expressions and visual and spoken cues

topics.title: Mediating meaning in and between languages

subtopics.title: Mediating meaning in and between languages

outcomes.text: locate, with support, key information in familiar texts and respond using gestures, images, words and modelled phrases
recognise that language carries cultural meaning in everyday social interactions
use words, familiar phrases and modelled language to create spoken, written and multimodal texts
recognise that [Language] has an oral tradition; and use the sounds and rhythms of [Language] to make meaning
recognise that [Language] has language conventions and grammatical structures, and has an oral tradition that can be represented in written form
notice that [Language] has features that may be similar to or different from English
recognise that [Language] and all Aboriginal languages and Torres Strait Islander languages belong to Country/Place and Peoples
notice that people use language in ways that reflect cultural identity
initiate exchanges and respond to modelled questions about self, others and the learning environment, using modelled expressions
participate in activities that involve planning with others, using a range of phrases and modelled structures in familiar contexts

topics.title: Mediating meaning in and between languages

subtopics.title: Mediating meaning in and between languages

outcomes.text: locate and respond to key information related to familiar content obtained from spoken, written and multimodal texts
develop strategies to comprehend and adjust [Language] language to convey cultural meaning
create and present informative and imaginative spoken, written and multimodal texts, using formulaic expressions, simple phrases and sentences, and modelled textual conventions
use combinations of sounds, pronunciation and intonation patterns of [Language] to form words and phrases
recognise and use [Language] language conventions, grammatical structures and syntax, in familiar texts and contexts
recognise familiar [Language] language features and compare with those of English, in known contexts
recognise that Aboriginal languages and Torres Strait Islander languages are passed down by Custodians, from generation to generation
identify connections among [Language] language, culture, Country/Place and identity
initiate and sustain modelled exchanges in familiar contexts related to Country/Place and students’ personal worlds
participate in activities that involve planning and negotiating with others, using language that expresses information, preferences and ideas

topics.title: Mediating meaning in and between languages

subtopics.title: Mediating meaning in and between languages

outcomes.text: locate and process information and ideas in a range of spoken, written and multimodal texts, and respond in different ways to suit purpose
apply strategies to interpret and convey meaning in [Language] language in non-verbal, spoken and written cultural contexts

create and present a range of informative and imaginative spoken, written and multimodal texts, using a variety of modelled sentence structures to sequence information and ideas, and conventions appropriate to text type
apply knowledge of combinations of sounds, syllables, pronunciation and intonation patterns to develop fluency and rhythm to known words, phrases and expressions
use knowledge of modelled grammatical structures and formulaic expressions to compose and respond to texts
compare some [Language] language structures and features with those of English, using some familiar metalanguage
understand how Aboriginal languages and Torres Strait Islander languages are maintained and strengthened
recognise that identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s) and Country/Place, and that this impacts on communication
initiate and sustain exchanges in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts related to Country/Place and students’ experiences, feelings and opinions, adjusting their language in response to others
collaborate in activities that involve the language of transaction, negotiation and problem-solving, to plan projects and events

topics.title: Mediating meaning in and between languages

subtopics.title: Mediating meaning in and between languages

outcomes.text: interpret and analyse information, ideas and opinions in a range of spoken, written and multimodal texts, and respond appropriately to cultural context, purpose and audience
interpret and adjust non-verbal, spoken and written language to convey meaning in [Language] language in familiar and some unfamiliar cultural contexts

create and present spoken, written and multimodal, informative and imaginative texts for specific purposes, selecting vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and features, and conventions appropriate to text type and context
apply knowledge of conventions of spoken [Language] to enhance fluency, and respond to and create texts, in familiar and unfamiliar contexts
apply understanding of grammatical structures and features to compose and respond to texts
reflect on similarities and differences between [Language] and English language structures and features, using metalanguage
reflect on how language conveys cultural knowledge, practices and norms
reflect on and explain how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), and Country/Place, and how these impact on communication
initiate, sustain and extend exchanges in a range of contexts related to students’ own and others’ experiences of the world, adjusting their language in response to others
contribute to discussions that involve diverse views to negotiate outcomes, address issues and compare experiences

topics.title: Mediating meaning in and between languages

subtopics.title: Mediating meaning in and between languages

outcomes.text: evaluate and synthesise information, ideas and perspectives in a broad range of spoken, written and multimodal texts, and respond appropriately to cultural context, purpose and audience
interpret and translate non-verbal, spoken and written interactions and texts to reflect cultural context, purpose and audience

create and present informative and imaginative texts for diverse contexts and purposes, selecting vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and a range of features and conventions to engage different audiences
apply features and conventions of spoken [Language] to extend fluency in response to a range of contexts, purposes and audience
apply knowledge of grammatical structures and features to predict meaning and compose a range of texts that contains complex structures and ideas
reflect on and evaluate [Language] texts, using metalanguage to analyse language structures and features
understand and apply protocols associated with language learning and language using in cultural contexts
reflect on and evaluate how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s) and Country/Place, and how these affect ways of communicating
